### 12.7 Replay: the trace re-drives the ordinary loop
- V1 This section specifies replay, re-running the ordinary loop on a recorded input trace.
- V2 A trace is the primary record of a session, a fixed trace header plus the batches drained at each frame.
- V3 A batch is a device's staged set of writes, and a device is any attached participant in the periphery.
- V4 A frame is one iteration of the loop, from drain to publication.
- V5 The drain is the frame-top swap that publishes staged device writes into the root inputs.
- V6 `replay!` is the entry point the §11.5 trace exists for: [§11.5]
- V7 [code block] trc  = trace(sim)                     # the recorded session: header + per-frame batches
- V8 The parts below cover the one substitution replay makes, halting and the input mode across halts, what stays the loop's, the validation up front, and the what-if replay with the `restore = false` form, which attaches the feed to the simulation as it stands.
- V9 The rejected shapes close the section.

#### One substitution
- V10 `replay!` is the ordinary loop with exactly one substitution, not a second loop (D-101, D-274). [D-101, D-274] (bold)
- V11 That is what keeps every property proved of the loop true of replay.
- V12 Its drain reads the trace, and under the default form the loop starts from a restored state.
- V13 The default form restores from the header.
- V14 `replay!` restores the trace's checkpoint (the `Model`'s state at a frame top as one value), the state the recording opened from.
- V15 It runs no boundary zero (the initialization boundary at `t₀`).
- V16 `replay!` stands in the `init!` position of the lifecycle (§12.6) and does what `restore!` does, with the trace header as the checkpoint (D-274). [§12.6, D-274]
- V17 There is no condition resolution, and the totality (§14.6) held when the recording's `init!` ran. [§14.6]
- V18 A condition is the datum that says "set this build to this state".
- V19 Whatever fired at `t₀` is part of the restored state, so nothing is applied twice and nothing is skipped (D-274). [D-274]
- V20 The drain reads the trace.
- V21 Each frame top applies the recording's batches for that frame ordinal, the frame index a batch replays at (D-101). [D-101]
- V22 It does not swap the staging cells of the roster (the list of attached device entries).
- V23 A staging cell is where a device's pending write batch waits between drains.
- V24 Ordinal keying is exact because the frame sequence is itself deterministic under replay (`t` boundaries derive from state, §10.4). [§10.4]
- V25 Frame k of the replay is frame k of the recording.
- V26 Recorded batches apply verbatim, with no surface re-check (D-101). [D-101]
- V27 The write-surface rule (§11.3) ran at recording time. [§11.3]
- V28 A write surface is the set of faces a writer's batch entries may reach, and a face is the name a port wears on its component's boundary.
- V29 Claims (the set of faces a device may write) are a live-roster fact of the recorded session that replay does not reconstruct.
- V30 A simulation is in one of two input modes, `:live` or `:replay`, and the mode decides which source that one drain branch reads (D-218). [D-218] (bold)
- V31 Under `:live` it reads the staging cells, and under `:replay` the attached recording.
- V32 `replay!` attaches the recording and enters `:replay` (D-218). [D-218] (bold)
- V33 `step!` and `run!` consume it from there, frame by frame, exactly as the drain paragraph above describes.
- V34 There is still one loop and one drain (D-218). [D-218]
- V35 A mode that outlives the call makes a partial replay a resumable position rather than the end of an operation (D-218). [D-218]
- V36 Whatever advances the simulation next reads the same mode and finds the same records.
- V37 That is what lets the reproduction workflow of §13.4 run through the ordinary entry points, with no replay-only spelling of `step!`. [§13.4]
- V38 That workflow halts at the frame top the error names, then `step!`s the failing frame on its recorded inputs.

#### Halting, and the mode across halts
- V39 In `:replay` the recording is the bound (D-218). [D-218]
- V40 Every advance's frame budget is capped at the recording's last frame, and `to_boundary = k` caps it earlier.
- V41 That keyword is the consumer of the replay pointer (§13.4). [§13.4]
- V42 `to_time` is the same cap addressed by time (below).
- V43 Either keyword names a frame from the one the feed starts from through the recording's last.
- V44 The feed starts from the header's frame under the default form, and from the simulation's own under `restore = false` (below).
- V45 Anything else is refused (`ArgumentInvalid`).
- V46 `to_boundary = k` takes the frame-entry boundary index (§13.4), a count of frame tops. [§13.4]
- V47 It is not the published-boundary ordinal that a snapshot (the immutable per-boundary publication) carries (§12.3). [§12.3]
- V48 Replay runs through frame `k` and halts exactly at the frame top after it (D-128). [D-128] (bold)
- V49 Replay therefore always halts at a frame top.
- V50 The frame-entry pointer (§13.4) lands the same way. [§13.4]
- V51 A localized `t` boundary inside the frame (the crossing instant bracketed by root-finding over trial sweeps) is reproduced but not stoppable-at (D-128). [D-128]
- V52 §10.4 separates the two indices. [§10.4]
- V53 The trace stays frame-indexed, and boundaries are the reporting index.
- V54 Replay may also end earlier still under the ordinary policies, since `t_end` and `ignore_stop_requests` are keywords of `replay!` exactly as of `run!` (§12.6, D-255, D-316). [§12.6, D-255, D-316]
- V55 A termination the recorded session hit through a stop request reproduces itself anyway, deterministically (D-127). [D-127]
- V56 A replay honours requests by default too, and the trace header records no policy.
- V57 So a replay of a live run that ignored some must pass the same `ignore_stop_requests`.
- V58 `to_time` addresses the same halt by time.
- V59 The keyword halts at the last frame top at or before the time given, and it is mutually exclusive with `to_boundary` (D-219). [D-219] (bold)
- V60 It computes `k = ⌊(to_time − t₀)/h⌋` against the header's `t₀`, under either form.
- V61 A time falling between two frame tops floors onto the earlier one.
- V62 The rounding is the deliberate opposite of `t_end`'s, which ends a run at the first grid boundary reaching or exceeding it (§12.4). [§12.4]
- V63 `t_end` bounds a run, and `to_time` positions an inspection.
- V64 The point of halting is to stand before the anomaly, so a halt that stepped past it would defeat the call (D-219). [D-219]
- V65 Validation is the other keywords'.
- V66 The value must be real, finite and at least `t₀`, and it must name a time the recording covers.
- V67 The checks run before the replay writes anything, the default form's restore included.
- V68 The halt flips the mode only at the recording's end.
- V69 A frame budget that runs out halts the loop at a frame top, leaving the simulation `initialized` (§12.6). [§12.6]
- V70 The mode becomes `:live` exactly when that halt lands at the recording's last frame, with the records exhausted (D-218). [D-218] (bold)
- V71 It stays `:replay` otherwise, and the next `step!` or `run!` goes on consuming the recording.
- V72 So no advance ever flips mid-run.
- V73 A `run!` whose `t_end` lies past the recording halts at the last recorded frame, now `:live`, and the next call is the live continuation (D-218). [D-218]
- V74 `live!` is the one call that moves the mode alone.
- V75 The flip above is automatic, and it happens only at the recording's end.
- V76 `live!(sim)` performs it by hand.
- V77 `live!` sets the mode to `:live` and detaches the recording's remainder, touching nothing else (D-219). [D-219] (bold)
- V78 The trajectory stands where the replay left it, and so does the trace with its header, inherited under the default form.
- V79 The next `run!` or `step!` is therefore the live continuation from the replayed boundary, and its drains append to the re-recorded prefix.
- V80 `live!` is a stopped-sim operation, legal only on an `initialized` simulation in `:replay`.
- V81 Every other state refuses under the ordinary lifecycle gates (§12.6), with `MissingInit` at `built` and `ServiceLifecycle` in the rest. [§12.6]
- V82 A simulation already `:live` refuses too, with `ArgumentInvalid`.
- V83 The call would have nothing to do, and a loud refusal beats a silent no-op (D-219). [D-219]
- V84 That call is what makes the rewrite workflow real.
- V85 An interactive session is interrupted at t = 110, and the last ten seconds are to be flown again:
- V86 [code block] trc  = trace(sim)                     # the interrupted session, out to t = 110
- V87 The trace `sim2` leaves behind is a complete recording of itself, the replayed prefix out to t = 100 and then the frames flown live after it.
- V88 A replay's halt leaves the simulation `initialized`, never `stopped` (D-218). [D-218] (bold)
- V89 That state is boundary-consistent and ready to advance, the same state `step!` leaves (§12.6). [§12.6]
- V90 This is what makes three promised workflows real (D-101). [D-101]
- V91 State-trajectory inspection asks "what was the private state at t = 37.2?", and answers it by replaying there and reading the live stores (§11.2). [§11.2]
- V92 Error reproduction replays to the frame-entry boundary `k` the error names, then `step!`s the failing frame under instrumentation (§13.4). [§13.4]
- V93 Continuation is `run!` after `replay!`, a live session from the replayed boundary.
- V94 After a full replay that is the next call, the records exhausted at the halt.
- V95 After a partial one the remainder of the recording is consumed first, across as many `step!` and `run!` calls as the caller makes, and the session goes live at the recording's end.
- V96 Or `live!` drops that remainder, and the continuation starts at the halt.

#### What stays the loop's
- V97 Replay re-records (D-101). [D-101] (bold)
- V98 The drain records normally.
- V99 Under the default form the new trace inherits the old header and accumulates the re-drained batches, a bit-identical prefix.
- V100 Under `restore = false` the new trace's header is the simulation's own checkpoint (below).
- V101 A replayed-then-continued session therefore leaves behind a complete, valid trace of itself, with no special stitching.
- V102 Pacing and the control plane are unchanged (§10.7, §12.1, D-101). [§10.7, §12.1, D-101] (bold)
- V103 The control plane is the separate atomic surface carrying pause, pace and the stop word.
- V104 Pacing (waits inserted between completed frames, never altering the boundary sequence) sits outside the semantics, so paused, slow-motion or real-time replay is free.
- V105 Paced replay with an attached visualizer is session playback, and `replay!` takes `pace` and `margin` as `run!` does (§12.1, D-269). [§12.1, D-269]
- V106 Stop truncates, as anywhere.
- V107 Devices are readers (D-218). [D-218]
- V108 Rostered devices init and spawn normally (§11.1) and consume snapshots (§11.2, §12.3). [§11.1, §11.2, §12.3]
- V109 That is the visualizer case.
- V110 But no live staging cell is drained while the simulation is in `:replay`.
- V111 A batch found staged is discarded with a rate-limited warning (`ReplayDiscardedStaging`, Appendix C). [Appendix C]
- V112 Mixing live writes into a replay would destroy the property replay exists to provide.
- V113 A session that wants live input is a continuation (`run!` after replay), not a replay.

#### Validation up front
- V114 Validation is loud and up front (D-101). [D-101] (bold)
- V115 Before the first frame, the checkpoint's deployment (the scalar-free artifact the grid parameters fix) is compared against the target's.
- V116 Its fingerprint, the structural layout, is compared against the `Build`.
- V117 The fingerprint covers the store layout, the root-input faces, and what a copy by position relies on (§11.5). [§11.5]
- V118 The root inputs are the root component's own input faces.
- V119 The trace's batch entries are validated against the root input-face list, and each batch's frame ordinal against the recording's frames, from the one after the header's to the last (D-217). [D-217]
- V120 Each writer's face-name → position schema, on the trace's `schemas` list (§11.5), is validated in the same pass. [§11.5]
- V121 A recorded schema that disagrees with the target model's own root-input faces is a replay error.
- V122 The checks are attach-style, and a failure reports did-you-mean, the offending name plus the list-in-hand it should have matched.
- V123 The kinds are `CheckpointMismatch`, `ReplaySchemaMismatch` and `ReplayUnknownFace` (Appendix C). [Appendix C]
- V124 The pass runs under both forms of `replay!`.
- V125 The same pass pays the trace-record conversion in reverse.
- V126 Every writer's sparse records (§11.5) are normalized to positional batches against the trace's `schemas` list, once, off the loop (D-176). [§11.5, D-176]
- V127 Replay has the whole trace in hand before frame 1.
- V128 The replay drain therefore applies compiled scatters exactly as the live drain does, and no face name is resolved per frame under replay either.
- V129 Structural mismatch is an error.
- V130 Parametric difference is not (D-101). [D-101]
- V131 The checkpoint check compares two deployments as values (D-254). [D-254] (bold)
- V132 The checkpoint carries the recorded run's `Deployment`, the target simulation's `Model` carries its own, and the check is their comparison, on the structural side of that line.
- V133 The value covers the trajectory-determining parameters, `Δt_base`, `h`, `N_base`, the algorithm, `localization_tol`, `localization_budget` (§10.4) and `firing_budget` (§10.6, D-133). [§10.4, §10.6, D-133]
- V134 It also covers the schedule (the typed per-component `(D, Φ, Δt)` tick table) with every column, the anchor and rate-chain columns included.
- V135 A rate re-declared through a different anchor at the same tick table is therefore a different deployment, and the replay is refused.
- V136 The refusal costs one re-recording in a rare case, and it keeps the equality a plain value equality rather than one that ignores two of a row's columns.
- V137 Mismatch is `CheckpointMismatch` with a deployment-parameter discriminator, never a what-if (D-127). [D-127]
- V138 A deployment change moves the times at which the frame-ordinal batches apply.
- V139 That is different inputs, not a modified model.
- V140 The event trio (the localization pair and `firing_budget`) is compared for exactly the same reason the grid parameters are.
- V141 It moves the trajectory, so a run that differs in it is not re-driving the recorded one.
- V142 Comparison by value is what makes the check one expression rather than a field-by-field walk.
- V143 Under the default form the clock is restored, not compared.
- V144 Replay restores `t₀` with the rest of the clock, so `replay!` takes no `t0` argument (D-127). [D-127]
- V145 Under `restore = false` the simulation's own clock runs, its origin must equal the recording's, and the new trace's header is the simulation's own checkpoint.
- V146 The checkpoint holds no policy (D-255). [D-255]
- V147 `t_end` and `ignore_stop_requests` are keywords of this `replay!` call, validated per call as at `run!`.
- V148 The dispositions, by trace content:
- V149 the checkpoint's fingerprint: store layout, root-input faces, and what a copy by position relies on
- V150 compared against the `Build`
- V151 the recorded `Deployment`, carrying `Δt_base`, `h`, `N_base`, the algorithm, `localization_tol`, `localization_budget`, `firing_budget`
- V152 compared as a value against the deployment the target simulation's `Model` carries
- V153 each writer's face-name → position schema (on the trace's `schemas` list)
- V154 validated against the target model's root-input faces: disagreement is a replay error
- V155 the checkpoint's state
- V156 restored under the default form; no boundary zero
- V157 the clock
- V158 restored under the default form, `replay!` takes no `t0`; under `restore = false` the simulation's own clock runs, its origin equal to the recording's
- V159 `t_end`, `ignore_stop_requests`
- V160 absent from the checkpoint; each `replay!` call declares its own (§13.5) [§13.5]

#### What-if replay and `restore = false`
- V161 Replaying against the same structure with changed parameters is the what-if replay, the deterministic re-driving of the recorded inputs through a modified model.
- V162 It is spelled as `init!` of the modified model under the authored condition, then `replay!(sim, trc; restore = false)`.
- V163 The trace is not self-sufficient for it.
- V164 Its checkpoint holds the recording model's state after boundary zero, so the authored condition comes from outside (D-274). [D-274]
- V165 Bit-identity is promised only against the identical build (§2.4). [§2.4]
- V166 What-if replay promises determinism, never reproduction.
- V167 `replay!(sim, trc; restore = false)` attaches the feed to the simulation as it stands and restores nothing.
- V168 The simulation must be `initialized`, at the recording's `t₀`, and at a frame from the header's to one short of the recording's last.
- V169 A simulation that is not `initialized` meets the lifecycle gate.
- V170 One whose origin or frame is off the recording's is refused before any write as `CheckpointMismatch`, its clock arm.
- V171 One grid is thus an invariant of every replay, and `to_time` has one meaning.
- V172 The drain applies the records from the frame after the simulation's own.
- V173 This form is a door like the default one, an entry point that builds a run (§12.6). [§12.6]
- V174 It builds a fresh run under the recording keywords, takes the simulation's own checkpoint as the new trace's header, and publishes one snapshot.
- V175 That form serves the what-if of a modified model initialized under the authored condition (above).
- V176 It also serves a seek, `restore!` of a checkpoint the recording passed through followed by the feed from the next frame (D-274). [D-274]

#### Rejected shapes
- V177 Three shapes are rejected for the record (D-101). [D-101]
- V178 They are a `run!(sim; replay = trc)` flag, a synthetic playback device staging the recorded batches, and replay ending `stopped`.
- V179 The input mode clarifies that decision's drain substitution rather than replacing it, and carries its own rejected shapes (D-218). [D-218]
- V180 ---
